- **★ A ruling delivered to a dark desk is indistinguishable from no ruling.** All three "Will-gated blockers" I would have read out at boot had been **ruled 8 days earlier**. - **★ A transfer completes when the RECEIVER encodes.** REG-15 sat owned by **nobody** for 7 days: the sender's half is self-motivated, the receiver's half has **no trigger at all**, and **both desks' own ledger checks pass clean** because each correctly audits only its own book. → auto-memory `finding_transfer_completes_only_when_the_receiver_encodes`.
- **★★ `consumer_check.py` SILENTLY DROPS hits on the best-maintained rows — reconcile every run against a plain grep.** REGINALD found my run reported **2** live stale hits where **5** existed; I reproduced the mechanism. `has_marker()` suppresses a hit whenever a supersession word appears nearby **without checking what the word REFERS to** — so a row documenting its own history (*"v2.3: EV $73.92 … (Prior v2.2.1 — EV $68.93 — superseded)"*) has the marker governing the **historical** value while the **live** one beside it is dropped. ⚠️ **The bias runs the wrong way: the better-maintained the row, the more likely it is ignored** — the dropped hit was his Convergence Matrix WAL row, the single line a reader consults for my state. **My careful screening of the reported list could not recover what was dropped before I saw it.** → packet to PROME/HENRY; auto-memory `finding_supersession_marker_suppresses_the_live_value_beside_it`. **Standing practice on this desk from now on: grep after every consumer_check, and trust the grep on disagreement.**
- **★ A peer mirroring MY version number breaks silently on every bump I make.** REGINALD's `CLAUDE.md` hardcoded *"thesis v2.3"*; he de-versioned it rather than bumping to v2.4 so it cannot rot again. **Worth asking at each publish: who mirrors my version token?**
- **★ Screen a consumer-check hit for SERIES before packeting it.** 6 raw hits → **2 genuine**, **2 false positives on coincidental digits** (a BXP share price and a HENRY market-data value, both literally `68.93`), **2 correct-as-history** (dated KB/research records — "fixing" those would destroy the calibration trail). **A live surface carrying a superseded number is a defect; a dated record carrying it is the audit trail.**
- **★ A defect fix and a judgment call must never share a fence.** fence-② froze weights pending a *judgment*; read as also freezing a cell corrupted by a *data defect*, it would have preserved a number refuted at 18 of 18 quarters. **Ask what a freeze was written to prevent before applying it to something new.**
- **★ The anti-ratchet constraint has a letter and a purpose, and they come apart.** Folding bear-fast's weight into bear-medium keeps total bear flat — satisfying the letter — while letting a disconfirmed premise's probability survive under a different name. **When a constraint is satisfiable two ways, ask which one the constraint was written to force.**

hit: - **★ Check that a rule's named instrument CAN carry its datum — three WAL rules have now failed this.** (1) MI3 is not a 10-Q line (DEWEY 7/16); (2)
context:
- **★ Verify a claim's SOURCE TIER before letting it move a score.** V3 was cut 2/5 → 1/5 on an A2 call paraphrase ("the book is shrinking") when the same quarter's A1 filing shows every line growing. The call may have meant something narrower — but the score moved on the paraphrase, not on the measure. **A convergence score should cite the instrument it can be re-tested against.**
- **★ Absence in a filing is not disconfirmation when a materiality blanket exists.** Note 15 says only that lawsuits are *"of a routine nature … will not have a material impact."* A $25M counterclaim against $98.7B of assets fits inside that. So the 10-Q **cannot distinguish "no counterclaim" from "an immaterial counterclaim."** What it *does* establish — management does not treat it as material — is the real datum. Say which one you have.
- **★ Silence about a transaction priced AT carrying value is structurally uninformative.** The second $60M LOI would produce no gain, loss or charge-off if it closed at ~carrying value, hence no disclosure. Non-disclosure is equally consistent with "closed cleanly" and "never closed." **Before reading a filing silence as evidence, ask whether the event would have been disclosable at all.**
- **★ Check that a rule's named instrument CAN carry its datum — three WAL rules have now failed this.** (1) MI3 is not a 10-Q line (DEWEY 7/16); (2) "Q3 10-Q **Schedule O**" — Schedule O is a *Call Report* schedule; (3) v2.3.1 leg (a) names the 10-Q for **consensus EPS**, which no filing carries. All three are *unfalsifiable by construction*, not merely unmet. Validity and executability are orthogonal axes — test them separately.
- **★ State the denominator whenever citing a coverage ratio.** WAL's headline "ACL/NPL 96%" is really *(funded + unfunded ACL) ÷ **nonaccrual***. On the full **NPL** base it is **69.1%**; on funded ACL ÷ NPL, **62.4%**. Three defensible denominators, and the headline is the most flattering. The company's own highlights make the same slip in the other direction (labelling a nonaccrual ratio "nonperforming").
- **★ A cluster of same-day 13G filings can be a legal-entity restructuring, not flow.** Two Vanguard LLCs at 5.01% and 5.02%, same signatory, same day, event date a month prior, both passive — and **both naming the same affiliates**, so the percentages are **not additive**. A naive EDGAR-feed read scores "two new 5% holders" as accumulation. **Check filer CIK vintage, event date, rule cited, and affiliate overlap before treating a 13G as a position change.**
- **★ Form 4 alone under-covers a departing officer.** Section 16 obligations end at departure, so an ex-officer's liquidation surfaces ONLY on Form 144 — exactly where WAL's most on-thesis insider datum was (Curley, $878K, 6/15, no Form 4). **Always pull 144 with 4.** Evidentiary limit: a 144 is notice of a *proposed* sale, not proof of execution.
